BackstoryDef.title: Blackwater smallholder
BackstoryDef.description: They grew food near the Blackwater, supplying villages and the endless appetite of King's Landing.

BackstoryDef.title: King's Landing smith's apprentice
BackstoryDef.description: Their forge repaired tools and weapons for customers ranging from dockworkers to armed retainers.

BackstoryDef.title: Dockworker's child
BackstoryDef.description: Raised among wharves, ropes, warehouses, and ships, they learned that the capital never stopped building.

BackstoryDef.title: Flea Bottom performer
BackstoryDef.description: Songs, jokes, tricks, and quick hands earned enough coppers to survive another day in the capital.

BackstoryDef.title: Red Keep ward
BackstoryDef.description: Placed at court as a noble ward, they learned that listening carefully was often safer than speaking.

BackstoryDef.title: Crownland heir
BackstoryDef.description: Their tutors prepared them to manage land in the shadow of the Iron Throne and its ever-changing politics.

BackstoryDef.title: Second son of the Blackwater
BackstoryDef.description: With an elder sibling set to inherit, they sought a future among household guards, knights, or royal service.

BackstoryDef.title: Waters-born bastard
BackstoryDef.description: Bearing the Crownlands bastard name Waters taught them to navigate the distance between noble blood and noble privilege.

BackstoryDef.title: Kingswood poacher
BackstoryDef.description: They became skilled at finding game in royal woods while becoming equally skilled at avoiding royal foresters.

BackstoryDef.title: Gold Cloak runner
BackstoryDef.description: As a youth attached to the City Watch, they carried messages, fetched equipment, and saw the aftermath of countless street fights.

BackstoryDef.title: Blackwater market farmer
BackstoryDef.description: They grew produce for the vast markets of King's Landing, where almost anything could be sold for the right price.

BackstoryDef.title: Capital armorer
BackstoryDef.description: The city's knights, guards, sellswords, and criminals ensured that metalwork was never short of customers.

BackstoryDef.title: King's Landing builder
BackstoryDef.description: They repaired houses, warehouses, walls, docks, and whatever had most recently burned down.

BackstoryDef.title: Kingswood hunter
BackstoryDef.description: Whether serving a noble hunt or quietly poaching, they know the forests surrounding the capital intimately.

BackstoryDef.title: Court painter
BackstoryDef.description: Portraits and decorations introduced them to nobles who preferred flattering art to accurate art.

BackstoryDef.title: Street chirurgeon
BackstoryDef.description: They treated workers, sailors, guardsmen, and victims of the capital's frequent violence.

BackstoryDef.title: Royal clerk
BackstoryDef.description: Years of petitions, tax records, legal orders, and sealed messages taught them how royal bureaucracy actually functioned.

BackstoryDef.title: Gold Cloak veteran
BackstoryDef.description: Service in the City Watch exposed them to riots, thieves, political purges, and the occasional command best left unquestioned.

BackstoryDef.title: Crown steward
BackstoryDef.description: They handled supplies, servants, coin, and correspondence for a household closely tied to King's Landing.

BackstoryDef.title: Red Keep courtier
BackstoryDef.description: They learned to survive court through charm, gossip, fashion, and knowing when not to repeat what they had heard.
